turnover_financial.text: main objective of the project is to collect evidence on WTR practices implemented by companies in the European Union, whilst also presenting a comprehensive overview of initiatives undertaken by governments and social partners aimed at altering the organisation and duration of working time. Additionally, the project will assess the benefits and the disadvantages that can arise from WTR both at an individual and firm level. Specifically, the project will investigate impacts on workers’ health and well -being, work-life balance, wages, working conditions, skills development and on firms’ revenues, costs, productivity, work organisation, turnover, training and recruitment practices, experiences of labour shortages and on workforce composition. The contribution resulting from this tender will add to a wider range of deliverables investigating WTR from different angles. The research programme under the SLA encompasses five interconnected research activities: I. An extended systematic literature review and policy update covering all EU -27 Member States, synthesising recent evidence on individual and organisational outcomes of working time reduction, with a particular focus on productivity effects and EU-relevant sources; II. references_experience.text: years, Europe has witnessed a gradual decline in the number of working hours. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). Afte r 1973, the decline in working hours slowed and became more varied across countries, with minimal reductions in the European Foundation for the Improvement of Living and Working Conditions 240105/7807 Procurement documents – Part B: Tender Specifications Page 12 of 40 average working week. Any reductions in working time at national level since the mid -1990s were largely driven by shifts in labour force participation and the rise in part -time work, resulting from more women entering the labour market. Background information Over the last 150 years, Europe has witnessed a gradual decline in the number of working hours. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). Le DUME est un formulaire européen unifié remplaçant la déclaration implicite sur l'honneur. Le DUME est une déclaration du soumissionnaire concernant la situation financière, les compétences et l'adéquation des entreprises à une procédure d'appel d'offres. Le DUME constitue une preuve provisoire que le soumissionnaire remplit toutes les conditions pour la sélection qualitative. Si le soumissionnaire a déjà fourni un DUME à l'autorité contractante dans le passé, il n'aura pas à le compléter à nouveau dans la mesure où l'information reprise dans ce DUME n'a pas été modifiée. Le soumissionnaire doit alors préciser le dossier pour lequel il a précédemment soumis un DUME. turnover_financial.text: main objective of the project is to collect evidence on WTR practices implemented by companies in the European Union, whilst also presenting a comprehensive overview of initiatives undertaken by governments and social partners aimed at altering the organisation and duration of working time. Additionally, the project will assess the benefits and the disadvantages that can arise from WTR both at an individual and firm level. Specifically, the project will investigate impacts on workers’ health and well -being, work-life balance, wages, working conditions, skills development and on firms’ revenues, costs, productivity, work organisation, turnover, training and recruitment practices, experiences of labour shortages and on workforce composition. The contribution resulting from this tender will add to a wider range of deliverables investigating WTR from different angles. The research programme under the SLA encompasses five interconnected research activities: I. An extended systematic literature review and policy update covering all EU -27 Member States, synthesising recent evidence on individual and organisational outcomes of working time reduction, with a particular focus on productivity effects and EU-relevant sources; II. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). Afte r 1973, the decline in working hours slowed and became more varied across countries, with minimal reductions in the European Foundation for the Improvement of Living and Working Conditions 240105/7807 Procurement documents – Part B: Tender Specifications Page 12 of 40 average working week. Any reductions in working time at national level since the mid -1990s were largely driven by shifts in labour force participation and the rise in part -time work, resulting from more women entering the labour market. Background information Over the last 150 years, Europe has witnessed a gradual decline in the number of working hours. Between 1870 and 1973, the average number of annual hours worked per worker decreased by over a thousand hours in nations like Germany, France, Italy, and the Netherlands. This decline in the number of working hours/days is driven by different factors, including key legislative milestones (for instance the introduction of the 40 -hour work week in developed countries through the ILO Forty -Hour Week Convention 1935 ), technological changes (for instance increasing automation and digitalisation of tasks), and new social aspirations (for instance the growing preference among workers for better work-life balance), amongst other elements (European Commission, 2023). submission.text: ..... ........ 3 Postbox Response Creation ................................ ................................ ................................ ............ 7 Late Postbox Submissions................................ ................................ ................................ ............. 12 Supplier User Guide - Postbox Page | 3 What is the Postbox? The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. Please note: Before you can use the postbox you must record your interest in a notice. In the case of a Quick Quote or the second stage of a dual stage procedure you must have been invited by the buyer to submit a response. Postbox Response Workspace All postbox re

Supplier Control Panel. Supplier Control Panel It can also be accessed by clicking the “Go to Postbox” button when viewing the notice in your interest list or Quick Quote list. Supplier User Guide - Postbox Page | 4 Notice Details – Interest List The Response Workspace is provided in two tabs – Notice Response List and Dispatched List. The Notice Response List shows all the current notices – contract notices, stage 2 notices, quick quotes – associated with your registration, which have the Postbox option activated. Notices will appear on this list until the deadline for submissions has passed. Le DUME est un formulaire européen unifié remplaçant la déclaration implicite sur l'honneur. Le DUME est une déclaration du soumissionnaire concernant la situation financière, les compétences et l'adéquation des entreprises à une procédure d'appel d'offres. Le DUME constitue une preuve provisoire que le soumissionnaire remplit toutes les conditions pour la sélection qualitative. Si le soumissionnaire a déjà fourni un DUME à l'autorité contractante dans le passé, il n'aura pas à le compléter à nouveau dans la mesure où l'information reprise dans ce DUME n'a pas été modifiée. Le soumissionnaire doit alors préciser le dossier pour lequel il a précédemment soumis un DUME.
